## Root cause confirmed — the gate measures the ticket store, not the code checkout

Investigation reproduced CI locally within pack-transfer variance: **648,346 KiB** local against Actions' **648,505 KiB**.

### The pack is not the code

| Fetch shape | size-pack KiB | Share of failing pack |
|---|---:|---:|
| main-only, blobless, full history | 23,268 | 3.6% |
| tickets-only, blobless, full history | 624,881 | 96.4% |
| all-heads, blobless, full history | 648,346 | 100% (reproduces CI) |

`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml` checks out with `filter: blob:none` and `fetch-depth: 0`. The unbounded depth pulls every remote head, including `origin/tickets`. The authorship gate then measures that combined pack and fails closed.

Composition of the failing pack by object type:

```
blob    count=5098    disk_kib=24605.6     3.8%
commit  count=296468  disk_kib=56059.5     8.6%
tree    count=518053  disk_kib=553579.0   85.4%
```

Tree objects are 85.4% of it, and the tickets-only blobless fetch contains **zero blobs**. This is the event-sourced ticket store's directory graph, which is exactly what an append-only store accumulates.

### It is not a large file, and not organic growth

The four largest blobs across all heads total roughly 1.7 MiB; all blobs together are 24.0 MiB. No single-artifact removal can address an 85 MiB overage. The top 30 ticket tree objects are 9,514 KiB — 1.47% of the pack. The cost is the accumulation of 494,742 tree objects, not any one object.

### The crossing was a discrete history event, not a growth curve

| Point | size-pack KiB |
|---|---:|
| 2026-09-04 | 482,385 |
| 2026-09-09 | 496,077 |
| 2026-09-10 18:30Z | 496,938 |
| **2026-09-10 19:00Z** | **598,124** |
| 2026-09-17 12:57Z | 624,751 |

Baseline growth is ~2.5 MiB/day before and ~3.9 MiB/day after. Between 18:30Z and 19:00Z on 2026-09-10 the pack gained **101,186 KiB in about 30 minutes**. The commit at the jump, `924a93f21edf6c4066339feeb7fff2294244d917` (`chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run 34514936676]`), is not a descendant of the commit before it and makes **28,570 previously-unreachable commits** reachable, the oldest dating to 2026-08-29.

This matters for the fix: extrapolating a new limit from a growth rate would be fitting a line to a step.

### This repository already learned this lesson

The Gerrit-side workflow carries an explicit note against the very gate that is failing here:

```
NOTE: there is deliberately NO pack-size gate here. A hard cap on the tickets
pack ... is guaranteed to be crossed eventually and, once crossed, casts Verified -1
on EVERY Gerrit change repo-wide until someone bumps the number.
```

The scheduled authorship gate has the same property, differing only in blast radius. `d0bcd620278` already raised this limit once from 102400 to 563200 and described it as a temporary bridge; the comment still says to restore 102400. That is the second crossing of a cap whose input is an append-only store, which is the predicted behaviour rather than a surprise.

The limit is not single-sourced in a `.github/*-limit.txt` file. It lives in the workflow and is mirrored by a contract test at `tests/unit/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py:101`, so any change must move both.

### Not done, and deliberately so

The reconciler behaviour that made run `34514936676` introduce 28,570 older commits non-linearly was not traced to source. The Git evidence establishes the event and its pack impact; the code path did not get read. Filed separately so it is not lost inside this gate fix.

No `git gc`, `repack`, `prune`, or `fsck` was run. All measurements come from fresh scratch clones.

comments.author: Joe Oakhart
comments.body:
## Tickets-branch remedy investigation: all scoped options measured, none is growth-class

Read-only measurement against throwaway scratch clones. Every option that stays inside the
tickets branch has now been quantified. Recording the full result so the next session does not
re-litigate any of these from intuition.

### Baseline

Clone carries 293,207 commits, 9,389 ticket dirs, 140,369 live event files, 494,949 reachable
trees. The CI pack exceeds the configured limit; the deficit is roughly 85,146 KiB.

### Options measured and rejected

| Option | Measured outcome | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Archival | Saves **0 KiB**. Archived tickets stay on the live branch with directory, history, marker and `ARCHIVED` event intact. Only 7 exist. | Dead |
| Ordinary compaction | Only **13,550 / 140,369 files (9.7%)** eligible across 3,893 tickets. Replaces eligible tip files with a `SNAPSHOT` and leaves all historical trees reachable; tip tree entries stayed ~421,254. | Not a tree remedy |
| Additional sharding | Structurally worse. Flattening needs a format migration *plus* rewrite to affect the current pack. | Dead |
| Orphan re-root, history retained off the fetched namespace | **Passes the gate** at 507,825 KiB with 55,375 KiB headroom, and `refs/archive/*` is empirically not fetched. But it buys ~**14 days**, needs a **biweekly global writer freeze**, and breaks authorship verification and op-cert anchors. | Dead |
| Folding enrich telemetry into compaction | **0 KiB immediate reclamation.** The types are deliberately non-replay. | Dead as an immediate remedy |
| History rewrite | Trees 494,949 -> 9,389; tree disk 93,759.5 -> 13,211.2 KiB = **80,548.3 KiB saved, against an 85,146 KiB deficit**. | May not even clear it |

### Why re-rooting is dead, precisely

Authorship verification resolves each event's introducing commit and validates key-era rules
**through commit ancestry**. Op-cert terminal signature material anchors to the tickets-branch
commit that introduced it and validates that anchor through ancestry too. An orphan root makes
every inherited event look introduced by the orphan commit, so the remedy for the authorship
gate's pack failure breaks the authorship gate's semantics.

The same objection applies to a filter-repo style rewrite, which changes every SHA and so
invalidates the same anchors. Combined with the fact that it saves less than the deficit, the
rewrite option is worse than it first appeared.

### Why the enrich types cannot simply be folded

`reducer/_version.py` defines `_NON_REPLAY_KNOWN_TYPES` and explicitly lists `REVIEW_RESULT`,
`ENQUEUE_ENRICH`, `CLAIM_ENRICH`, `DONE_ENRICH`. The stated contract is that unknown/non-replay
records must be preserved so an older clone cannot destroy data written by a newer clone;
`docs/event-schema.md` documents the same guarantee. The queue module adds a second rationale:
the event store is deliberately used as a durable broker-free queue, and the retained stream is
what makes leases and retries correct after a crash.

Adding these to `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` is therefore not a configuration tweak. It would make them
reducer state and change the compatibility contract.

### The actual growth driver

| Type | Files | Logical KiB |
|---|---:|---:|
| `ENQUEUE_ENRICH` | 26,037 | 31,070.7 |
| `CLAIM_ENRICH` | 29,299 | 34,536.6 |
| `DONE_ENRICH` | 24,922 | 28,240.5 |
| `REVIEW_RESULT` | 9,205 | **233,243.1** |
| **Total** | **89,463** | **327,090.9** |

That is **63.8% of live event files**, and `REVIEW_RESULT` alone is **71% of that payload** at
roughly 25 KB per record. The dominant consumer of tickets-branch storage is the gate system's
own review sidecars. Plan review and code review each write a durable record, so gate usage is
self-amplifying with respect to this failure.

Note the logical byte figures are uncompressed content, not pack contribution. Git delta
compression and shared trees make per-path pack attribution invalid, which is why no residual
MiB/day is claimed here.

### Known prior fan-out

The code documents a 2026-08 event where reconcile churn re-fired enrichment roughly 15x per
ticket and grew the tickets branch roughly 10x. Debouncing reduces future churn but does not
remove retained history.

### Consumers that block a latest-only design for `REVIEW_RESULT`

`metrics.sidecar_metrics` sums `llm_calls` across **all** review records and pairs historical
errors with later passes. Plan-review calibration and regression mining read the retained
corpus. Remediation sidecar receipts are audit material. A latest-only snapshot would break
each of these, so `REVIEW_RESULT` needs an aggregate-plus-retention design rather than folding.

### Conclusion

No tickets-branch-scoped remedy both reclaims enough pack now and changes the growth class.
Immediate relief requires history rewriting, which is destructive, insufficient on its own, and
breaks authorship and op-cert anchors. A durable fix requires a bounded-retention or
off-branch-placement design for queue telemetry and, separately, for `REVIEW_RESULT`.

Mitigating context for prioritisation: this gate is **schedule-triggered and not in the
`Verified` hot path**, so today it is recurring noise rather than a merge blocker.

## Correction: the pack is NOT growing, the bridge budget is already blown, and authorship verification has been offline for days

Three measurements taken from the failing CI runs themselves, which change this ticket's
framing and supersede the "headroom runway" analysis posted earlier.

### 1. The pack is flat, not growing

`checkout pack is N KiB` read from five separate failing runs:

| Run created | Pack (KiB) |
|---|---|
| 2026-09-15T12:57Z | 650,044 |
| 2026-09-16T07:01Z | 647,945 |
| 2026-09-17T01:13Z | 647,738 |
| 2026-09-17T18:56Z | 648,166 |
| 2026-09-18T07:00Z | 647,498 |

Across three days of heavy ticket writing the pack moved by **−2,546 KiB** — down, not up.
There is no growth curve and therefore no deadline. Every remedy I measured earlier was
scored against reclaiming *future growth headroom*; that was the wrong question. The
problem is a **static overage**, and it has been static for at least three days.

### 2. The bridge budget is already exceeded

`verify-identity.yml:34` sets `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 563200`, and its own comment
explains the number: "temporarily 563200 for the ~481 MiB blobless tickets pack … Restore
102400 after the pack measures below that limit."

The pack now measures **~632 MiB against a bridge sized for ~481 MiB**. The W3 bridge
(`a8ba`, closed) is not merely insufficient to reach the 100 MiB target — it no longer
holds the current pack at all.

### 3. The gate has not verified anything since at least 2026-09-15

This is the part that matters most, and it is not "noise". The pack check is the step
**immediately after checkout**, before `setup-python`, before `Install rebar`, and before
the authorship verification itself. It fails closed. So for 12 consecutive runs the
authenticated-authorship gate has exited before verifying a single event.

The lane is not producing a weak signal — it is producing **no signal**, while looking like
a failing test. Whatever assurance this gate is supposed to provide about mutating events
against the ancestry-scoped keyring, the project has not had it since 2026-09-15.

### 4. My earlier remedy exploration duplicated `536b`'s already-decided design

`536b` (`polite-antivirus-bedbug`) already owns this, with an operator decision recorded
2026-08-24 (Option 2, remote-anchored horizon, N=30d) and a C1–C5 safety boundary. Its
description also already states the two results I re-derived independently:

- "`git gc`/repack does NOT shrink it (proven)" — matches the flat curve above.
- "`.retired` files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless ⇒ `.retired` GC shrinks it ~0"
  — this is exactly why my archival measurement returned **0 KiB**. I reported that number
  as a discovery; it was a re-derivation of a known result.

`536b` further quantifies the achievable win: N=30d ≈ 365–380 MiB, N=7d ≈ 200–215 MiB, and
"≤100 MiB needs an unsafe <4-day horizon" — so a temporary budget raise is unavoidable, and
the structural fixes are W1 (batch the enrichment/digest write lane) and W2 (shard the flat
ticket dirs to cut root-tree churn), both already carved out of that epic.

The decision I escalated from this ticket was therefore malformed: it offered a choice among
remedies when the sanctioned remedy already exists, is designed, and is in progress.

### Consequence for this ticket

The useful scope left here is not "pick a reclamation strategy". It is the gap between now
and `536b` landing: the authorship gate is dark, and the bridge budget no longer matches
reality. That is a scoping decision for the operator, not something to resolve by measuring
more remedies.

Correction to this ticket's "Why this matters" section, and the sharper scope it implies.

That section says the gate being red means "no commit's authorship is being verified". That is wrong, and I wrote it before checking how the Verified vote actually consumes this workflow.

`gerrit-verify.yaml` defines its **own** `verify-identity` job — "verify-identity (whole-store authorship gate)", at roughly line 499 — and that job is what `vote.needs` aggregates into the Verified vote. It performs the same whole-store authorship walk and it does **not** contain the pack-size budget. That is why changes have continued to earn `Verified +1` throughout this outage, and it means pre-merge authorship verification has never stopped.

What is actually lost is narrower and still real: the standalone `verify-identity.yml` lane — push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, and the every-6-hours schedule — is the **periodic whole-store sweep**, and it has produced no authorship verdict on any run since 2026-09-15. A change that lands green can still be contradicted later by store-wide state the pre-merge walk did not see; the scheduled sweep is what would catch that, and it has been silent.

The remedy is unchanged, and this correction actually reinforces the chosen approach. Because `verify-identity.yml` is a parity-governed source workflow (`scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py` requires every unconditional job in it to be folded into `vote.needs`), splitting the budget into a **second job** would have forced the pack overage into the Verified hot path, where it would have blocked every change. Deferring the verdict **within the single existing job** avoids that entirely. `check_verify_gate_parity.py` reports OK against the implemented change.

Implementation detail worth recording, because it is the part that is easy to get wrong: the pack is measured immediately after checkout and judged in the final step, rather than simply moved to the end. The `Mount tickets branch as a worktree` step fetches the event log into the object database, so a measurement taken after it would be a materially larger quantity than the budget was ever calibrated against. Moving the whole check to the end would have silently changed what is under budget while appearing to preserve it.

Change 2987 implements this. Five structural tests pin the ordering by parsing the workflow rather than observing a CI run, so they hold under any CI provider and under none; four of the five fail against the previous ordering, and the fifth asserts the fail-closed invariant that must hold either way.

Remaining unverified: acceptance criteria 1, 2 and 5 require a run log from this lane, which cannot exist until the change lands. Once it merges I will trigger the lane via `workflow_dispatch` and attach the step conclusions showing the authorship verdict reported alongside a still-failing pack budget.

Pre-close audit of the acceptance criteria, done against the staged fix so the close gate is not the place these are discovered.

**Status: 0 of 5 checked.** Two can be proven from the diff now; three require a real CI run and are correctly still open.

**AC3 — limit unchanged, failure condition unchanged: EVIDENCE HOLDS.**
`REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 563200` does not appear as an added or removed line in `git diff origin/main...HEAD`, so the value is untouched. The comparison survives the step split intact: the judging step still runs `if (( SIZE_PACK_KIB > REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB )); then … exit 1`. Same operator, same direction, same fail-closed exit. The only change is that the measured value now arrives through `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` as `SIZE_PACK_KIB` instead of being a shell local in the same step. The measuring step is itself fail-closed: its `awk` exits 1 if no `size-pack:` line is found, so a measurement that silently produces nothing cannot be read as zero.

**AC4 — no early-warning or monitoring mechanism added: EVIDENCE HOLDS.**
No added line in the diff matches warn, notify, alarm, monitor, sns or cloudwatch. The change reorders and splits existing steps; it introduces no new signalling path.

**AC1, AC2, AC5 — not checkable yet, by design.**
All three assert observed behaviour of a real run: that authorship verification executes and reports its own verdict on a run whose pack is over budget (AC1), that the pack check still fails the job on a genuine overage (AC2), and that the authorship verdict is legible without expanding a failed step (AC5). The commit has not been through CI. Checking these from the diff would be asserting an outcome rather than observing one, so they stay open until the change is green.

Scope note: the commit touches 4 paths, while `file_impact` still declares 1. Widening it is deliberately deferred until the change lands, because CI feedback could still alter the file set and each widening invalidates the plan attestation.

## All 5 acceptance criteria now have evidence. The remedy behaves exactly as designed.

Change 2987 merged as `e900fa14ad5`. `verify-identity.yml` ignores pushes to `main`, so the merge
triggered no run; a `workflow_dispatch` run was fired against `main` to produce the evidence:
run `35410257116`, head `e900fa14ad5`, conclusion **failure**.

That failure is the intended outcome, and it is the proof. The step list:

```
Run actions/checkout@v7                                    success
Measure the blobless checkout pack                         success
Install rebar                                              success
Mount tickets branch as a worktree                         success
verify-identity (gating)                                   success
verify-opcert (required-environment op-cert gate)          success
Fail closed if the blobless checkout pack exceeds its limit  FAILURE
```

**AC1 — authorship executes and reports its own verdict on an over-budget run: MET.** The pack was
over budget on this very run, and the authorship step still ran to its own conclusion and printed
its verdict:

```
verify-identity: advisory — enforcement is off
(43993 signed (not era-verified in advisory mode), 228 unsigned; 44221 event(s) in scope).
```

Before the fix this step was never reached, because the budget check aborted the job first. This is
the first authorship verdict the standalone lane has produced since 2026-09-15.

**AC2 — the pack check still runs and still fails the job on an overage: MET.** Same run:

```
##[error]checkout pack is 648416 KiB; limit is 563200 KiB
```

The judging step is the only failing step and the job conclusion is `failure`. The gate did not
become permissive; it became correctly ordered.

**AC3 — limit and failure condition unchanged: MET.** Recorded earlier from the diff and confirmed
in the run environment, which shows `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 563200`. The judging step still
runs `if (( SIZE_PACK_KIB > REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB ))` with the same operator, same
direction, and the same fail-closed `exit 1`. The measuring half is itself fail-closed: its `awk`
exits 1 when no `size-pack:` line is found, and the judging half refuses an unmeasured value with
`the checkout pack was never measured; treating as a failed budget check`, so a silent
non-measurement cannot be read as zero.

**AC4 — no early-warning or monitoring mechanism added: MET.** Recorded earlier from the diff; no
added line matches warn, notify, alarm, monitor, sns or cloudwatch.

**AC5 — the authorship verdict is legible without expanding a failed step: MET.** `verify-identity
(gating)` appears in the run's step list with its own `success` conclusion, distinct from and ahead
of the failing budget step, so the authorship outcome is readable from the step list alone.

### `file_impact` corrected

It declared 1 path against the merged commit's 4. It now declares all 4:
`.github/workflows/verify-identity.yml`, `tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone.py`,
`tests/integration/test_ci_tickets_partial_clone_workflows.py`, and the new
`tests/unit/test_identity_gate_step_order_f5ac.py`. That widening invalidates the plan attestation,
so a fresh plan review runs before the close — after the criteria boxes are ticked, not before,
since ticking edits the description the review pins.

### Residual, not part of this ticket

The pack is 648416 KiB against a 563200 KiB limit, so the standalone lane still ends red on the
budget. That overage is the separate concern tracked by `0894-b9b8-6590-4904`, which owns restoring
the limit to 102400 once the pack measures below it. This ticket's defect — the budget pre-empting
the authorship verdict — is fixed.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

The scheduled `Verify Authorship Identity` workflow fails on every run. Confirmed still
failing on the 5 most recent runs through 2026-09-18T18:55Z (head `e12d60a76`).

The failing job is `verify-identity (authenticated-authorship gate)`; the failing step is
"Fail closed if the blobless checkout pack exceeds its limit". The error is exact:

```
checkout pack is 647650 KiB; limit is 563200 KiB
```

with `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB: 563200` in the step environment.

## Why this matters

This is the authenticated-authorship gate. The pack check is the **second step in the job**,
ahead of `setup-python` and the install, so when it fails the authorship verification never
executes at all. The gate is not failing authorship — it is aborting before reaching it.

What is lost is the **periodic whole-store sweep**. Pre-merge authorship verification has NOT
stopped: `gerrit-verify.yaml` defines its own `verify-identity` job, which performs the same
whole-store walk, carries no pack budget, and is what `vote.needs` aggregates into the Verified
vote — which is why changes have kept earning `Verified +1` throughout this outage. The standalone
`verify-identity.yml` lane — push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch and the every-6-hours schedule —
is the sweep that would catch store-wide state a pre-merge walk did not see, and it has produced no
authorship verdict since 2026-09-15. A standing red scheduled run also trains readers to ignore the
gate.

## Root cause (established)

Legitimate growth, not debris. The blobless pack is dominated by the tickets branch history.
Reducing it is the subject of `0894-b9b8-6590-4904`, which tracks restoring the budget to
100 MiB once the `536b` history reclaim lands. The pack overage is therefore a known,
separately-owned condition — not this ticket's defect.

This ticket's defect is narrower and is the one causing the loss of signal: **a size
precondition is ordered ahead of the gate's actual purpose**, so an unrelated budget overage
silently disables authorship verification.

## Decision

Operator decision, 2026-09-18: reorder the job so authorship verification runs and reports
its own verdict first, with the pack check retained, still fail-closed, after it.

Explicitly rejected alternatives:

- Raising the ceiling again — makes the bound track the pack instead of constraining it.
- Removing or softening the pack check — it is a deliberate safeguard and stays fail-closed.
- Adding an early-warning monitor for pack growth — does not restore the lost signal.
- Scoping the pack reduction outside the tickets branch — that is where the growth is, and
  it is owned by `0894`.

The job is expected to remain red on the pack step until `0894` lands. That is the correct
outcome: the budget is genuinely exceeded. What changes is that authorship verification
executes and reports, so the gate produces its signal again.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Authorship verification executes and reports its own pass/fail verdict on a run whose
      pack exceeds `REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB`, verified by a run log showing the
      authorship step's result on such a run.
- [x] The pack check still runs and still fails the job when the pack exceeds the limit,
      verified by that same run log showing the job conclusion is failure and the pack step
      reports the overage.
- [x] The pack limit value is unchanged at 563200 and the pack step's failure condition is
      unchanged, verified by the diff.
- [x] No early-warning or monitoring mechanism is added, verified by the diff.
- [x] The authorship verdict is legible without expanding a failed step — its outcome is
      visible in the run's step list, verified by quoting the step conclusions.

file_impact.reason: Splits the pack budget into a measuring step and a judging step, and moves the judging step after the authorship verification, so an over-budget pack can no longer pre-empt the authorship verdict. The limit value and the fail-closed comparison are unchanged.
Updates the partial-clone integration expectations for the split pack steps, including the measured value now arriving through GITHUB_OUTPUT as SIZE_PACK_KIB.
Updates the workflow-level partial-clone assertions for the same step split.
New test pinning the step order: the authorship verification must run before the pack-budget judgement, so the budget cannot pre-empt the verdict.
